evidence_level: L2 (real firmware + 6DOF plant + sensor models, SIL only)
purpose: Scan real outage altitude after climb completion, crossed with 1/2/3 m/s target-altitude ramp; avoid the earlier confound where --alt was a target and the vehicle was still climbing at outage.

matrix.timing: pos_hold_at = alt + 11 s; outage_start = alt + 13 s; outage_end = start + 20 s; run = end + 50 s

caveats: Middle of the touchdown distribution is soft (0.85-1.12 m/s) for all rates; the safety-relevant tail is not. At 20-40 m the 2/3 m/s arms have p95 3.8-6.5 m/s, worse than 1 m/s at 30/40 m.
Faster ramps reduce drift substantially at 20-40 m (e.g. 30 m median 530 -> 259/266 m, p95 1617 -> 450/468 m) but do not improve touchdown safety.
The 40 m H/W 1 m/s cells drift ~1.3 km: 40 s of 1 m/s² wind with no horizontal absolute reference. This is physical drift, not filter divergence.
SIL plant has no aerodynamic drag, ground friction, landing gear, or impact absorption. Touchdown speeds are kinematic.
The remaining deficiency is the landing phase (no flare/touchdown detection), not the target ramp rate.
All numbers are scalar-Eigen SIL L2, not real aircraft.

A ground-dwell latch (target=current altitude after 1 s below 0.3 m) was added after these runs. It changes only post-touchdown target/throttle behavior; land_t/land_hold/land_vz_down/max_roll_preland are measured before it applies and are unaffected.
